subject: social
source: NCERT Democratic Politics II (Class X Political Science), Chapter 2

topics.name: What makes India a federal country?

questions.q: Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between…
questions.a: a central authority and various constituent units
w: the President and the Prime Minister
questions.e: Usually two levels – one for the whole country, the others for provinces/states.

questions.q: The distinguishing feature of a federal government is that…
questions.a: governmental power is divided between different levels of government
w: the national government gives some powers to provinces
power is divided among legislature, executive and judiciary
questions.e: NCERT exercise 8: division between levels.

questions.q: Which is an example of a ‘coming together’ federation?
questions.a: USA
questions.e: USA, Switzerland and Australia were formed by independent states coming together.

questions.q: Which is an example of a ‘holding together’ federation?
questions.a: India
questions.e: India, Spain and Belgium – a large country divides power between states and the national government.

questions.q: Under a unitary system…
questions.a: there is only one level of government, or sub-units are subordinate to the Centre
w: states have powers of their own
two levels are separately answerable to the people
questions.e: In a federal system, the Centre cannot order a state government to do something.

questions.q: In ‘holding together’ federations…
questions.a: the central government tends to be more powerful and units may have unequal powers
w: all states have equal power and are strong
states can leave whenever they like
questions.e: Some units may be granted special powers.

questions.q: Who acts as an umpire if disputes arise between different levels of government in a federation?
questions.a: The highest court
questions.e: Courts interpret the constitution and the powers of each level.

questions.q: How many of the world’s 193 countries have federal political systems, according to the chapter?
questions.e: Only 25 countries, but their citizens make up 40% of the world’s population.

questions.q: In which year did Belgium shift from a unitary to a federal form of government?
questions.e: In 1993 regional governments were given constitutional powers no longer dependent on the Centre.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a federation, the fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be changed by one level of government alone.
Reason (R): The existence and authority of each tier is constitutionally guaranteed.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: Changes need the consent of both levels because each tier’s authority is guaranteed.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Sri Lanka is a federation.
Reason (R): Sri Lanka is divided into provinces.
questions.a: A is false, but R is true.
w: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
questions.e: A is false – Sri Lanka is, for all practical purposes, unitary; having provinces alone does not make it federal.

questions.q: Which of these is on the Union List?
questions.a: Defence
questions.e: Union List: defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications, currency.

questions.q: Which of these is on the State List?
questions.a: Police
questions.e: State List: police, trade, commerce, agriculture, irrigation.

questions.q: Which of these is on the Concurrent List?
questions.a: Education
questions.e: Concurrent List: education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption, succession.

questions.q: If a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflict…
questions.a: the law made by the Union Government prevails
questions.e: Union law prevails in case of conflict.

questions.q: Subjects like computer software that are not in any list are called…
questions.a: residuary subjects, and the Union Government legislates on them
questions.e: The Union has power over residuary subjects.

questions.q: How can the power-sharing arrangement between Union and States be changed?
questions.a: Passed by both Houses of Parliament with at least two-thirds majority and ratified by at least half of the State legislatures
w: By a simple majority in the Lok Sabha
By an order of the Prime Minister
questions.e: Parliament cannot change it on its own.

questions.q: Which states enjoy special powers under Article 371?
questions.a: Assam, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
questions.e: Due to peculiar social and historical circumstances – protecting land rights, culture and preferential employment.

questions.q: Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Delhi are examples of…
questions.a: Union Territories
questions.e: Too small to be States; the Central Government has special powers in running them.

questions.q: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
questions.a: Local governments – Residuary powers
w: Central and State governments – Concurrent List
questions.e: Residuary powers belong to the Union Government (NCERT exercise 10).

questions.q: What was the first and major test for democratic politics in India?
questions.a: The creation of linguistic States
questions.e: It actually made the country more united and administration easier.

questions.q: Which of these States was created on the basis of culture, ethnicity or geography rather than language?
questions.a: Uttarakhand
questions.e: Nagaland, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand.

questions.q: What is the status of Hindi according to the Constitution?
questions.a: The official language – India has no national language
w: The only language for all official work
A Scheduled Language only in Delhi
questions.e: Hindi was identified as the official language; no language was made the national language.

questions.q: How many languages are recognised as Scheduled Languages by the Constitution?
questions.e: Hindi plus 21 others are in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.q: Use of English for official purposes was to stop in 1965. What happened instead?
questions.a: After demands from non-Hindi states (violent in Tamil Nadu), English was continued along with Hindi
w: Hindi was imposed on all states
questions.e: The flexibility of leaders helped India avoid a situation like Sri Lanka’s.

questions.q: What changed in Centre-State relations after 1990?
questions.a: Regional parties rose and coalition governments began at the Centre, leading to more respect for state autonomy
w: One party ruled the Centre and all States
The Centre began dismissing more state governments
questions.e: A Supreme Court judgement also made arbitrary dismissal of state governments difficult.

questions.q: According to the 2011 Census, Hindi is the mother tongue of about what share of Indians?
questions.a: About 44 per cent
questions.e: No single language is the mother tongue of a majority of Indians.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The formation of linguistic States made India more united.
Reason (R): It ensured that people who spoke the same language lived in the same State and made administration easier.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: Experience proved the fear of disintegration wrong; R explains why.

questions.q: When power is taken away from the Central and State governments and given to local government, it is called…
questions.a: decentralisation
questions.e: The third tier of government.

questions.q: In which year was the Constitution amended to make the third tier more powerful?
questions.e: Regular elections, reservations, State Election Commission, sharing of powers and revenue.

questions.q: What proportion of positions in local bodies are reserved for women?
questions.a: At least one-third
questions.e: There are now more than 10 lakh elected women representatives.

questions.q: Who conducts panchayat and municipal elections?
questions.a: The State Election Commission
questions.e: An independent institution in each State.

questions.q: The head of a municipal corporation is called the…
questions.a: mayor
questions.e: Municipality → chairperson; municipal corporation → mayor.

questions.q: The gram panchayat works under the overall supervision of the…
questions.a: gram sabha, made up of all the voters in the village
questions.e: The gram sabha meets at least twice or thrice a year to approve the budget and review performance.

questions.q: A few gram panchayats grouped together form a…
questions.a: panchayat samiti (block or mandal)
questions.e: All panchayat samitis in a district form the zilla parishad.

questions.q: Which city in Brazil combined decentralisation with participative budget-making?
questions.a: Porto Alegre
questions.e: About 20,000 people take part every year; Kerala has tried something similar.

questions.q: Which is a difficulty that still remains in local government in India?
questions.a: Gram sabhas are not held regularly and states have not transferred enough powers and resources
questions.e: We are still a long way from realising the ideal of self-government.

questions.q: Who conducts panchayat and municipal elections according to the passage?
questions.a: The State Election Commission
questions.e: An independent State Election Commission was created in each State.
questions.passage: A major step towards decentralisation was taken in 1992. The Constitution was amended to make the third tier of democracy more powerful and effective. It is now constitutionally mandatory to hold regular elections to local government bodies. Seats are reserved in the elected bodies and the executive heads of these institutions for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes. At least one-third of all positions are reserved for women. An independent institution called the State Election Commission has been created in each State to conduct panchayat and municipal elections. The State governments are required to share some powers and revenue with local government bodies.

questions.q: What share of positions in local bodies is reserved for women?
questions.a: At least one-third
questions.e: ‘At least one-third of all positions are reserved for women.’

questions.q: Which statement from the passage shows that local government got real resources?
questions.a: State governments must share some powers and revenue with local bodies
w: Seats are reserved for SC, ST and OBC
questions.e: Powers and money (revenue) make local government effective.

questions.q: Why were safeguards needed to protect languages other than Hindi?
questions.a: Hindi is the mother tongue of only about 40 per cent of Indians
w: Hindi was declared the national language
questions.e: Imposing Hindi on the rest could have caused conflict (as in Sri Lanka).
questions.passage: Our Constitution did not give the status of national language to any one language. Hindi was identified as the official language. But Hindi is the mother tongue of only about 40 per cent of Indians. Therefore, there were many safeguards to protect other languages. Besides Hindi, there are 21 other languages recognised as Scheduled Languages by the Constitution. A candidate in an examination conducted for the Central Government positions may opt to take the examination in any of these languages.

questions.q: How many languages besides Hindi are recognised as Scheduled Languages?
questions.e: Hindi + 21 others = 22 Scheduled Languages.

questions.q: Which is NOT a feature of federalism?
questions.a: The Union government can change the powers of the States on its own
w: There are two or more levels of government
Each level has its own jurisdiction set by the Constitution
Courts interpret the Constitution and the powers of each level
questions.e: Fundamental provisions cannot be changed by one level alone.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a ‘holding together’ federation?
questions.a: India
questions.e: Holding together: India, Spain, Belgium. Coming together: USA, Switzerland, Australia.

questions.q: What is the dual objective of a federal system?
questions.a: To safeguard the unity of the country and accommodate regional diversity
w: To give all power to the Centre
To make one language official everywhere
questions.e: Mutual trust and agreement to live together are needed for both.

questions.q: Education, forests, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession are on which list?
questions.a: Concurrent List
questions.e: Both Union and State can make laws on them.

questions.q: If a State law and a Union law on a Concurrent List subject conflict, which prevails?
questions.a: The Union law
w: Neither – the courts decide a new law
questions.e: On Concurrent subjects, the law made by the Union Government prevails.

questions.q: How can the power-sharing arrangement between the Union and the States be changed?
questions.a: By a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament, ratified by at least half of the State legislatures
w: By an order of the Prime Minister
By a simple majority in the Lok Sabha
questions.e: This makes the arrangement very hard to change.

questions.q: What did the experience of forming linguistic States show?
questions.a: It made the country more united and administration easier
w: It ended the use of Hindi
questions.e: Fears that language States would divide India proved wrong.

questions.q: Why did the relationship between the Centre and the States change after 1990?
questions.a: Regional parties rose, coalition governments were formed and the Supreme Court made it hard to dismiss State governments arbitrarily
w: The Constitution abolished the State List
All States came under one party
questions.e: This brought a new culture of power sharing.

questions.q: What does the Gram Sabha do?
questions.a: All village voters meet at least twice or thrice a year to approve the gram panchayat’s budget and review its performance
questions.e: The panchayat works under the overall supervision of the gram sabha.

questions.q: Who elects the members of a panchayat samiti (block/mandal)?
questions.a: All the panchayat members in that area
w: All adult voters of the district
questions.e: Gram panchayats are directly elected; the samiti is elected by the panchayat members.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Local government is a step towards deepening democracy.
Reason (R): It allows people to directly participate in decision-making on local issues.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.e: Local self-government brings decisions closer to the people.
